title: HVAC and AC Are Not the Same Systems
desc: If you need help choosing between an HVAC or AC system, contact Rosenberg Indoor Comfort in San Antonio today for expert advise!

blocks.text: There are a few differences between an HVAC and air conditioning unit. Many homeowners are confused by these two systems and how they operate. While they are different, many people do not know what separates them.

Many home builders and contractors will use “HVAC” and “AC” interchangeably. There is a difference in the way that both units operate and function in your home. The acronyms may confuse people, but they are two different systems for heating and cooling. A professional HVAC company will be happy to help you find the right kind of unit for your living space.

The term HVAC stands for heating, ventilation and air conditioning. The HVAC is responsible for cooling and heating your home or business. Its ventilation ducts allow the moisture to drain from the system. An HVAC system has a few components. The furnace, air conditioner, and vents all work together in an HVAC unit. While most HVAC units do include air conditioning, it is not uncommon to find an HVAC system without this component.

Air conditioning, or AC, is just used to cool down the air in your home. The term “AC” is often used for any unit that conditions the air systems, even if it cools or heats the air. For most contractors, however, the AC unit is the system that is designed to cool the air. A system that can heat the air and pull moisture through the ductwork is known as an HVAC unit.

In review, the air conditioning unit can only cool the air in your home. An HVAC unit can cool, heat and ventilate your home. Now that you know the difference, you can find the right system to install in your space.
